verification.scope: Execution and contract checks; business ambiguities require operator answers

notes: Sheet 'Variants' (13 rows incl. header, 11 columns, no merged ranges, no formulas/errors) was detected as a single table; it is the only sheet in the workbook.

Identity: one product record per SKU (12 unique). Product name and Parent style repeat 4x because each style has 2 colors x 2 sizes; Parent style is a grouping attribute, not the identity, per operator instruction.
Currency 'PHP' and Price list 'standard' are explicit in every row and are taken verbatim; no FX conversion is applied and no currency is inferred from brand or country.
'Tax included' = 'No' in all rows, so each price row is vat_included = false; this is stated in the source, not inferred from a retail convention.

'Tax rate' = 5% is an explicit source value (the operator notes these are fictional fixture rates); it maps to vat_rate 0.05 rather than the schema default 0.07. Flag for the operator only if 5% was meant as a display-only label.
'Net price' is carried into /prices/*/amount unchanged, preserving the 2-decimal precision of the source.
Color and EU size are mapped to attributes.color and attributes.size as instructed; Parent style is kept as attributes.parent_style so no source data is lost.

No barcode, category, description, warehouse/stock, promotion or date columns exist in this workbook, so /barcode, /category, /description, /inventory, /promotions and the effective_from/effective_to fields are left empty rather than guessed.
Price collection has a single member per SKU (identity /price_list + /effective_from); effective_from/effective_to are absent in the source and remain null.

tables.reason: Single sheet with one row per variant SKU (12 rows, SKU unique, no nulls). It carries product identity (SKU, Product name) plus variant attributes (Parent style, Color, EU size) and inline pricing fields (Currency, Price list, Net price, Tax included, Tax rate). Product identity lives here, so the table's primary role is products with an embedded single-row price block rather than a separate pricing table.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Header 'SKU'; unique per row (12/12), matches sku_like hint and the pattern STYLE-n-COLOR-SIZE used for variant identifiers.

columns.name: Product name
columns.reason: Header 'Product name'; 3 distinct descriptive values ('SIM court shoe 1..3') repeated 4x each, one per style, matching the product_name synonym list.

columns.name: Currency
columns.reason: Header 'Currency'; single value 'PHP' in all 12 rows, a 3-letter ISO code matching the target pattern ^[A-Z]{3}$. Used as-is, no FX conversion.

columns.name: Sales unit
columns.reason: Header 'Sales unit'; single value 'PAIR' in all rows, which is in the target enum_hint for sell_unit and normalizes cleanly via unit_normalize.

columns.name: Price list
columns.reason: Header 'Price list'; single value 'standard' in all rows, exactly the contract's default/example list name for the prices collection.

columns.name: Net price
columns.reason: Header 'Net price'; float, never empty, 12 distinct values 1234.56-1356.77 with monetary decimals, one value per SKU. 'Net price' appears in the amount synonym list.

columns.name: Tax included
columns.reason: Header 'Tax included'; boolean-ish 'No' in all 12 rows, directly the vat_included semantic, giving false without inference.

columns.name: Tax rate
columns.reason: Header 'Tax rate'; single source value '5%' with percent hint, so vat_rate = 0.05 via parse_number_th(percent_to_fraction). This is an explicit source value, used instead of the schema default 0.07.

columns.name: Parent style
columns.reason: Header 'Parent style'; 3 distinct codes (STYLE-1..3) each repeated over 4 variant rows, i.e. the style grouping above SKU. Not a record identity and not an explicit category, so it is retained as an extra attribute rather than mapped to /category.

columns.name: Color
columns.reason: Header 'Color'; 2 distinct short codes (BLK 6, WHT 6) embedded in the SKU. Operator instruction requires preserving it as attributes.color string.

columns.name: EU size
columns.reason: Header 'EU size'; integer values 40/41, 6 rows each, embedded in the SKU as its final segment. Operator instruction requires preserving it as attributes.size string.

changes_from_draft: Removed the three invalid field targets /attributes/parent_style, /attributes/color and /attributes/size: the schema only allows the object at /attributes, not per-key pointers. Those variant columns are now left unmapped and delivered by attributes_passthrough, with source headers renamed to 'color', 'size' and 'parent_style' so the attribute keys are attributes.color, attributes.size and attributes.parent_style as the operator asked.
/prices/*/price_list now reads the explicit 'Price list' column ('standard') instead of a hard-coded constant.

Added /prices/*/vat_rate = parse_number_th('Tax rate', percent_to_fraction) -> 0.05, an explicit source value rather than the schema default 0.07 (recorded as information, per the operator note that these rates are fixtures).
/prices/*/vat_included now parses the 'Tax included' column ('No' -> false) instead of a constant.
/currency mapping trimmed to real ISO codes and kept keep_unmapped so an unexpected code is never silently rewritten.
Added quality rules for sku not_null/unique, product_name not_null, currency pattern and positive price.

/status, /barcode, /category, /description, /unit/pack_size, /inventory, /promotions and the effective_from/effective_to dates are left unmapped: no source column supports them, so nothing was fabricated.
